name: Reel
text: Use Deepgram’s real-time transcription for the pending video. It’s the fastest way to get a full transcript, which directly feeds the link coverage goal. The trade-off is higher cost per minute compared to batch processing, but speed beats savings here.

name: Scriv
text: Deepgram’s real-time transcription isn’t the bottleneck—it’s the 14-day A/B test that risks locking us into a tool we can’t swap out. Skip it; batch-process with Whisper for now, then run the A/B test on the transcript quality, not the tool’s speed. Settle it by measuring error rates and turnaround time for both methods over 48 hours.

name: Chisel
text:
Run the 14-day fixed A/B test on 200k clips with Whisper batch processing. This keeps the test clean, repeatable, and free of real-time tool lock-in, which matters more than speed for measuring transcript quality. The trade-off is slower turnaround for the A/B test, but we avoid betting on Deepgram’s speed before proving its quality holds up.

name: Sift
text: The 200k-clip fixed A/B test with Whisper batch processing locks us into a slower, less flexible pipeline than real-time Deepgram—we’re trading *immediate* link coverage gains for a delayed, rigid experiment. Instead, run a *parallel* 48-hour A/B test on 10k clips: Whisper batch vs. Deepgram real-time, measuring error rates *and* turnaround time. If Deepgram wins on both, we scale it immediately; if not, we drop it without derailing the +5%/day coverage goal.

name: Scope
text: Run the 14-day fixed A/B test on 200k clips with Whisper batch processing. This keeps the test clean, repeatable, and free of real-time tool lock-in, which matters more than speed for measuring transcript quality. The trade-off is slower turnaround for the A/B test, but we avoid betting on Deepgram before proving Whisper’s quality at scale.

name: Scriv
text: The 14-day fixed A/B test on 200k clips isn’t just slow—it’s a gamble that delays link coverage gains while Deepgram’s real-time option proves the bottleneck isn’t speed but *tool lock-in risk*. Run a 48-hour parallel test on 10k clips: if Deepgram’s error rate and cost per minute meet Whisper’s within 2% margin, we ship real-time now; if not, we default to Whisper batch. That settles the argument in two days, not two weeks.
